candidates.change_summary: Replace return true with return false so successful execution returns false instead of true.
Replace require(_tos.length > 0) with require(_tos.length > 1) so calls with exactly one address revert instead of completing.
Replace require(_s) with require(!_s) so the function reverts when the external call succeeds and succeeds when it fails.
Insert return false after the for loop but before the original return true, causing early return of false if the loop completes (dead code after).
Move the return true statement to before the for loop, causing the function to return true immediately without executing transfers.
Delete the for loop body so no transfers are executed and return true is unconditional.
Change the condition from _tos.length > 0 to _tos.length == 0, which will revert on non-empty arrays and succeed on empty ones, altering the observable revert behavior.
Delete the require inside the loop that checks the success of the call, so the function no longer reverts if an external call fails, changing the revert behavior.

Replace `bytes4(keccak256("transferFrom(address,address,uint256)"))` with `bytes4(keccak256("transfer(address,uint256)"))`, causing a different function selector to be called on caddress and thus changing external call behavior and revert/success conditions.
Replace the loop condition `i<_tos.length` with `i<=_tos.length`, causing an out-of-bounds access to _tos and a revert on every call, altering revert behavior.
Delete the entire `require(_tos.length > 0);` statement, allowing calls with empty _tos to succeed (return true) instead of reverting, changing the revert/success behavior.
Change the return value from `true` to `false`, so the function returns false after completing the loop (or never reaching it), altering the boolean result observable by callers.
Replace `caddress.call(...)` with `from.call(...)`, changing the target of the external call and potentially altering success/failure and side effects.
